title: Ensemble embedding evaluator with temporal gold corpus and drift probes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reusable evaluation harness that runs ensemble-style offline embedding quality checks against a time-partitioned golden corpus. The harness should: (1) support multiple scoring metrics (Cosine, dot-product, MRR, Recall@K, normalized rank), (2) run temporal drift probes (sliding windows, synthetic perturbations, noise & paraphrase probes), (3) produce per-model and per-corpus telemetry suitable for Console charts and alerting, and (4) be able to run at scale on the nightly job platform or ad-hoc for PR validation. This ticket focuses on the harness scaffolding, a curated temporal gold corpus seed, and integration points for Console telemetry and CI gating.
tasks: Design schema for temporal gold corpus (date partitions, provenance metadata, label confidence)
Implement runner that computes: mean-similarity, batch-wise MRR, Recall@1/5/10, normalized rank distributions
Add synthetic perturbation module: token-drop, synonym-replace, sentence-reorder and their expected degradation baselines
Integrate runs with telemetry pipeline: produce per-run metrics and artifact links for Console ingestion
Create nightly pipeline configuration and resource estimate for scaling to 100k queries/day
Write PRD-level README and usage examples for engineers and PMs
Add PyPI-friendly python entrypoint and a lightweight Docker image for reproducible runs
acceptance_criteria: Harness computes full metric set and outputs canonical CSV/JSON artifact with provenance headers
Temporal gold corpus schema and an initial seed of 8k labeled pairs uploaded to S3 with access control
Nightly job runs without OOM on staging and produces metrics that the Console can ingest via telemetry API
Synthetic perturbation suite demonstrates expected relative metric drops for at least two model families
A GitHub Actions job exists to run a small smoke harness on each embedding-related PR
Documentation and runbook added: how to add new gold partitions, how to interpret drift alerts

notes: We intentionally separate corpus provenance from model outputs to make drift attribution clearer (corpus-change vs model-change).
Plan to include a small 'canary' partition sampled from synthetic user prompts to detect rapid regressions from model updates.
